title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's sequel to 'La Longue Marche', in the discrete setting of 'groupes à lacets' (L-groups). These are surface-type groups, essentially pi_1 of a surface of type (g,n), carrying a 'structure à lacets': a distinguished family of conjugacy classes of loop elements or subgroups (the cusp or boundary 'lacets'), possibly oriented.

The previous page defines a new kind of structure on a group Pi:
- a commensurability class of subgroups Pi_0 (any two meet in a subgroup of finite index in both, and the intersection is again admissible);
- given germs of homomorphisms K_i: T -> Pi (homomorphisms defined up to restriction to finite-index subgroups) are required to factor through Pi_0;
- the resulting set of germs of exterior homomorphisms into Pi_0 must come from a loop structure on Pi_0, uniquely determined once Pi_0 is chosen.

This page names such a structure an 'L.T.-structure'. Grothendieck first wrote 'méta-L…' (echoing 'métabélien') and crossed it out. L stands for 'lacets', T for 'Teichmüller'. L.T.-groups are 'mixtures' of Teichmüller groups (mapping class groups) and L-groups.

Illustration:
- Take an extension (6) 1 -> pi -> G -> T -> 1 in which pi carries an L-structure invariant under conjugation by G. Then G is an L.T.-group, with pi as a 'sous-groupe de définition': pi is a normal subgroup, typically of infinite index, carrying the loop structure.
- Canonical example (7): G = Aut_L(pi) and T = Autext_L(pi), the automorphisms and outer automorphisms preserving the loop structure.
- For pi a centreless (hyperbolic) surface group, Dehn–Nielsen–Baer identifies Autext_L(pi) with the (extended) mapping class group of the surface of type (g,n), i.e. the Teichmüller group. Aut_L(pi) is then the mapping class group with one extra marked point.
- So (6)/(7) is the Birman exact sequence 1 -> pi_1(S_{g,n}) -> Gamma_{g,n+1} -> Gamma_{g,n} -> 1 (up to labelling and permutation of punctures).
- The next page draws the conclusion: the Teichmüller group of the punctured surface, an extension of the Teichmüller group by the fundamental group, 'apparaît comme un LT-groupe'.

Purpose: to find a single axiomatic class of discrete groups containing both surface groups and mapping class groups. The class should be stable under such extensions, so that the whole Teichmüller tower (iterated Birman / configuration-space fibrations) can be handled uniformly. The loop/cusp data, the inertia, propagate through the fibre subgroups.
errors: The identification Inn(pi) = pi needed for 1 -> pi -> Aut_L(pi) -> Autext_L(pi) -> 1 requires pi to be centreless. This fails for the non-hyperbolic cases (pi = Z for the cylinder / twice-punctured sphere, Z^2 for the torus); the page tacitly assumes hyperbolic type.

The previous page's margin note already flags a gap: it is not clear a priori that the set of germs of exterior homomorphisms obtained is finite. The definition is therefore not yet shown to be well-posed.
The uniqueness of the loop structure on Pi_0 'une fois Pi_0 choisi', and its compatibility when passing to commensurable Pi_0', are asserted rather than proved.
Whether the axioms hold for the full Aut_L(pi) (including orientation-reversing automorphisms) depends on whether the lacets are oriented; this is left unspecified.

ideas.what: Definition of 'L.T.-groups': groups equipped with a commensurability class of 'definition subgroups', each carrying a loop (cusp) structure induced from given germs of homomorphisms; intended as a common generalization of surface groups and Teichmüller groups.
ideas.modern_name: Groups with peripheral structure / fibre subgroups with cuspidal structure; closest are the 'PSC-type' and configuration-space groups of combinatorial anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard notion; related frameworks by Hoshi–Mochizuki (combinatorial anabelian geometry, 2009–) and the classical Birman/Ivanov theory of mapping class groups
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses 'groupes à lacets' and Teichmüller groups, but the term 'L.T.-groupe' and this definition appear to be only in the unpublished sequel (unsure)

ideas.what: Extension 1 -> pi -> Aut_L(pi) -> Autext_L(pi) -> 1 exhibiting the mapping class group with an extra point as an extension of the Teichmüller group by the surface group.
ideas.modern_name: Birman exact sequence, combined with the Dehn–Nielsen–Baer theorem
ideas.where_published: The Teichmüller tower and its fibrations are discussed in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Using commensurability classes ('germs') of subgroups and of homomorphisms as the basic data, rather than fixed subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: Commensurators / germs of homomorphisms up to finite index
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in geometric group theory (e.g. Margulis, Mostow)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes an axiomatic class of 'L.T.-groups' that mixes loop-structured surface groups and Teichmüller groups. It is designed to be closed under extensions by loop-structured normal subgroups, so that the entire Teichmüller tower consists of L.T.-groups. The theory is started (definition, basic example) but its foundational issues are left open: finiteness of the germ set, uniqueness and compatibility of the induced loop structure.
missed.quote: j'ai envie ... d'appeler les groupes Π munis d'une telle structure-liée : une classe de sous-groupes discrets commensurables entre eux - des L.T.-groupes (où L est initiale de "lacets", et T de "Teichmüller")
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Hoshi–Mochizuki's combinatorial anabelian geometry studies exactly these iterated fibre groups of configuration spaces with cuspidal/inertia structure, with outer automorphism groups compared to GT-hat. A discrete axiomatic class of this kind, intended to include mapping class groups themselves, is a natural but apparently unformalized framework. It would treat Teichmüller groups and surface groups on the same footing for anabelian / Grothendieck–Teichmüller purposes.

deep.surprise_reason: The worked example is the classical Birman exact sequence. The new element is Grothendieck's proposed axiomatic notion ('L.T.-groupes') unifying surface groups with loop structure and Teichmüller groups via commensurability classes of definition subgroups. It is a modest, unfinished definitional idea not found in the literature under this form, though close in spirit to later combinatorial-anabelian frameworks.
transcription_corrections: 'où L est initiale de "locale"' should read 'où L est initiale de "lacets"' (L-groupes = groupes à lacets).
'(si π est un des groupes locaux)' should likely read '(où π est un groupe à lacets)' or similar; the handwriting is consistent with 'lacets', not 'locaux'.
'Partant des groupes locaux π' should likely read 'Partant des groupes à lacets π'.
The crossed-out word before 'groupes' is likely 'métab…' (an abandoned 'métabélien'-style coinage, as on the previous page), replaced by 'L.T.-'.
'structure - liée' is the end of 'structure-là' / 'structure liée' continuing from the previous page; the colon introduces the gloss 'une classe de sous-groupes discrets commensurables entre eux'.
